I will keep my full 9.2 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best, it fits my land and irrigation conditions, and it spreads my income across the year. Since some family members work off-farm and labor is limited, I will keep management practical and steady instead of trying anything risky. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few key times, and use rotary tillage because it is efficient for me. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield, then put more nitrogen on maize than wheat, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and keep pesticide sprays limited to necessary control. I will aim for stable production rather than the highest possible input level, because with 9.2 mu and my experience, I would rather protect yield and control costs.
